params.body:
## Why

A dealer types 48.500 km in "wagen toevoegen", closes the draft, opens it again from the list and finds **49 km**. Same for a weight: 1.300 kg becomes 1,3.

`OwnStockService::tempupdate` is the third way into the vehicle table, beside `finalizeCreate` and `finalizeEdit`, and it was the only one without their normalisation. The classic create page posts the form as the dealer reads it ("48.500", `Custom::wholeNumberInput`), and MySQL reads "48.500" into a double column as 48,5. The two save paths have run everything through `normaliseAmounts()` since the number boxes were made Dutch; the draft save never did.

Finding `2026-09-16-conceptfiche-herladen-schrijft-48500-als-48-5`, issue #612.

## What changed

`tempupdate()` applies the same `OwnStockService::normaliseAmounts()`: the kilometre boxes to whole numbers, the weights and taxes to plain floats, an empty amount box to `0.00`. Three doors, one way of writing a number. Nothing else moves: the POST the create page fires while loading stays as it is; it disappears with that page, once the Livewire sheet saves its draft everywhere (noted in the finding).

## Tests

`TempUpdateNormalisesAmountsTest` (3, `@rule S1-1.1`): a grouped reading survives the draft save, a typed decimal and a plain number both survive, and a box the form did not send is untouched. Mutation-checked: without the one line, two of the three fail with exactly the reported symptom (48500 → 48).

Run: `OwnStock|Vehicle|Temp` → 414 tests, 2168 assertions, one pre-existing skip. `php bin/rules-sources`: Geen problemen. R S1-3.18 now says every door reads the numbers this way, and the finding is resolved with its pull request.
params.title: The draft save writes the numbers like the other two doors
